title: Binary Tree Right Side View
keyIdea: From the right you see one node per depth: the rightmost. DFS right child first, carrying the depth; the first node reached at each depth (level == rightView.size()) is the one you see.

approaches.name: BFS: last node of each level
approaches.idea: Level-order with a queue; the node popped last in each level (i == levelSize − 1) is visible.
approaches.why: Every node is visited once; the queue holds about one level.

approaches.name: DFS right-first with depth
approaches.idea: solve(node, level): if level == rightView.size(), this is the first node at that depth → push it. Recurse right, then left.
approaches.why: Each node is visited once; the recursion is as deep as the tree.

quiz.q: Why does level == rightView.size() mean "first at this depth"?
options: rightView has one entry per depth already seen, so its size is the next new depth
It means the node is a leaf

quiz.q: Can a visible node be in a left subtree?
options: Yes, when the right side is shorter at that depth
